messages:
ana: noticed a spike in handshake failures across eu-west and ap-south after last night's rotator run. logs show KMS decrypt denies on a subset of proxies.

ana: here's the top-line from the edge logs: `tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate` and `kms: decrypt denied, principal=proxy-keystore-role`

devon: is this the RBAC change rolled out in the rotator PR? I saw a permissions tighten for `proxy-keystore-role` yesterday.

maria: yeah that PR removed the legacy keystore read for a few service accounts and switched to `keystore-accessor` role. the rollout was canary -> 30% -> 100% via the rotator.

kevin: can you paste the rotator job output? rotator-bot should have the job id. I want to check which instances rotated certs.

rotator-bot: rotator job 2026-03-15-03:45 completed. targets: edge-proxy-eu-west(30%), edge-proxy-ap-south(30%), fallback routes enabled.

ana: pulling job logs now. snippet: ```
2026-03-15T03:46:12Z INFO attempting kms unwrap for cert /keystores/edge-proxy-eu-west/instance-12
2026-03-15T03:46:12Z ERROR kms unwrap failed: AccessDenied
2026-03-15T03:46:12Z WARN fallback to cached cert allowed=false
```

maria: that `cached cert allowed=false` was supposed to be true for the canary to avoid outages. did the feature flag flip?
devon: feature flag `edge.cert.fallback` is true in config for eu-west canary group. but the rotator job shows `fallback=false`. maybe a rendering bug in the template.

kevin: another vector — the audit logs show the KMS deny came from a principal `svc-account@infra` not the expected `rotator@infra`. could be an IAM mapping issue after the RBAC change.

ana: posted quick grep of audit events: `auditbot: KMS.Decrypt Deny principal=svc-account@infra resource=projects/redwood/keys/edge-keystore reason=ttl-expired-role-binding`

auditbot: new alert -> 6 KMS.Decrypt denies in 2m across two regions. correlated with rotator job id 2026-03-15-03:45.

sre-oncall: spinning up a rollback for the rotator canary and enabling fallback via console. taking the canary group out of rotation.

maria: thanks. while we rollback, we should confirm the RBAC change diff: `git show origin/main:infra/iam/roles.yaml | sed -n '1,160p'` — I suspect a missing `iam:impersonate` binding for the rotator service account.

devon: i'm running `gcloud iam roles describe` and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` to validate. if the rotator is impersonating `svc-account@infra` but lost impersonate permission, KMS calls will show as the wrong principal.

kevin: good catch. also check the keystore replication lag — if a rotated cert wasn't propagated to fallback cache, `fallback=false` will cause immediate handshake failures.

ana: quick mitigation checklist I pushed to the incident doc: - rollback rotator canary - re-enable cached cert fallback globally for edge proxies - add KMS allow rule for `svc-account@infra` temporarily - validate keystore replication status - run synthetic handshakes 

maria: on replication: `replicatorctl status edge-keystore` shows 98% propagated, 2% pending (mostly ap-south). might be the pending ones failing KMS unwrap combined with RBAC denies -> 502s.

devon: after rollback we should run `curl --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:<proxy-ip> https://api.redwood.internal/healthz --tlsv1.3` from a canary client to exercise the TLS path. include `-v` to see cert chain.

kevin: also add permanent fix items: - failing test in CI to catch `kms:decrypt` principal drift - rotation template validation for `fallback` flag - IAM preflight to ensure impersonate bindings present before rotator runs.

ana: agreed. assigning tasks in the incident doc. tagging @sre-oncall for follow-up action and @security for RBAC postmortem.

sre-oncall: rollback complete, traffic reverted for canary. monitoring shows handshake errors dropping. continuing 15m watch.

maria: once green, we'll push a hotfix PR to reintroduce the `keystore-accessor` binding with explicit `iam:impersonate` for `rotator@infra`. will include unit test to validate template rendering for `fallback`.

devon: and we'll add an audit log alert that fires if KMS.Decrypt denies exceed threshold for a single rotator job id.

kevin: filing a vuln-triage ticket to track the temporary IAM exception and follow-up hardening. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4921

ana: thanks team. once the postmortem is written we'll include recommended TLS hardening: ensure TLS 1.3 only for internal edge, strict cert pin validation for service-to-service but a robust fallback strategy for rotation events.

rotator-bot: rotator job 2026-03-15-03:45 status: rolled back by sre-oncall. next scheduled run postponed.

maria: follow-up action items in incident doc: `SEC-VM-ROTATE-2026-03-checklist` — will add owners and ETA.
